ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 19020 as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-74 governing Yuhan Hoesa limited liability companies; Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; and the revised FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 as implemented through Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) examination and guidance standards.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Yuhan Hoesa registration certificate issued after court registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry Office, National Court Administration of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: issue the certificate, have any required signature notarized if the destination requires it, and obtain an Apostille certificate from the competent authority of the state of issuance. For non-member states of the Apostille Convention: issue the certificate, notarize if required, legalize it at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the state of issuance, and then complete consular legalization at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that state. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean equivalent: current certified corporate registration certificate showing existence and no pending liquidation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry Office, National Court Administration of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: obtain the certified corporate registration from the Korean court, then have the registration officer's signature apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; for use in Korea of a foreign equivalent, obtain the Apostille from the originating state's competent authority. For non-member states: notarize the document, legalize it at the originating Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then obtain consular legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction over the originating state. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney for incorporation and banking opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All incorporators or the corporate parent's board of directors, with notarization before a licensed notary public in the state of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: execute before a notary public in the state of execution, then have the notary's certificate apostilled by the appropriate competent agency of that state; if the document is executed in Korea, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues the Apostille. Consular legalization path: execute before a notary, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization from the executing state, then obtain legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that state. The two mechanisms are exclusive alternatives and cannot be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jung-Gwan) of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All incorporators and a Korean notary public if the Articles are executed in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the Articles are Korean documents intended for foreign use: notarize the execution signatures and obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise, after notarization, obtain Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization and then Korean Embassy or Consulate legalization for the foreign destination. For foreign-document versions used in Korea, apply the reverse rule with the originating state's Apostille or consular legalization. Never apply Apostille and consular legalization in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the parent, shareholder, or existing banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank maintaining the account and authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: the bank officer signs and notarizes the reference letter, and the competent authority of the issuing country issues an Apostille. Consular legalization path: notarize the bank officer's signature, legalize at the issuing country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then legalize at the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that country. These paths are mutually exclusive; only the path applicable to the issuing jurisdiction may be used.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The compliance protocol requires screening every UBO, director, officer, authorized signer, and any person holding 25 percent or more of the Yuhan Hoesa against: (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanctions lists; (iii) the European Union and United Kingdom consolidated sanctions lists; and (iv) Republic of Korea domestic sanctions, financial regulation, and export control lists published by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Financial Services Commission, and KoFIU. Politically exposed persons include foreign and domestic prominent public officials, their immediate family members, and close associates. Any PEP identification requires enhanced due diligence, source of funds and source of wealth analysis, senior management approval in writing, and ongoing transaction monitoring for red flags such as shell company structures, nominee shareholdings, opaque ownership layers, and rapid movement through payment rails. Re-screening must be completed within 90 days and after any material ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS (Internet Registration Office) of the Supreme Court of Korea, operating the commercial registration and corporate name search database; official service accessible via www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All Korean corporate names must be expressed in Hangeul script; a foreign-language name may only be used through phonetic transliteration into Hangeul, and the registered legal name is the Hangeul version. English and other foreign scripts are not separately registerable as the statutory name. The four-tier naming convention consists of: (1) the mandatory legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; (2) a distinctive Hangeul trade name; (3) an optional phonetic transliteration of a foreign trade name; and (4) an unofficial English parallel name used in contracts, invoices, and international payment systems.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed Hangeul trade name because it is identical to an existing Korean corporation, the applicant should promptly amend and refile an incorporation application with a sufficiently distinguishable trade name; an appeal will not change an identity-based rejection. If the rejection is based on an asserted statutory prohibition or an improper refusal to register on procedural grounds, Korean counsel should obtain the written rejection decision and file an immediate objection or appeal before the competent District Court under the Non-Litigation Case Procedure Act within the statutory appeal period. If the District Court dismisses the objection, the applicant may pursue administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act. Because the disputed name may remain unavailable during an appeal, parallel filing of a new name application is strongly recommended to avoid incorporation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only if it is a genuine serviced office with a physical workstation, a valid local lease, and not a post-office box or bare commercial correspondence address. Korean courts may accept a Hongsil (serviced office) as the registered seat, but the National Tax Service and Korean banks often reject a pure mailbox address for VAT registration, corporate bank account opening, and recurring external audit confirmation. For the target LegalTech SaaS business using Stripe and credit card payment rails, the safer approach is a physically staffed shared office in Seoul, operating as the venue for business records, director meetings, and National Tax Service correspondence, because a phantom address materially raises bank rejection risk and triggers enhanced due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection risk is quantitatively assessed at approximately 15 percent during the first 12 months for a clean low-risk SaaS entity; the risk rises to about 35 percent if the registered address is shared by three or more unrelated corporations. The mandatory physical inspection checklist for the Korean authorities includes: (1) a visible company sign at the registered seat; (2) a physical presence of the director, employee, or registered agent during business hours; (3) maintenance of the corporate seal, statutory books, VAT records, and accounting documents at the address; (4) no more than three legal entities appearing under the same unit address; (5) in-place utility invoices or a lease agreement in the company name; and (6) a valid telephone listing available for National Tax Service contact.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Law No. 1000, as amended), particularly Part II, Chapter I, Articles 287, 289, 290, 292, 295, 312, 317, 329, 331, 335, 382, 383, 389, 393, and Chapter III, Articles 553 to 567, concerning a Yuhan Hoesa; together with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the Notary Act, the Registration of Non-Contentious Cases Act, and the Local Tax Act for registration taxes.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea, including the Supreme Court of Korea electronic registration portal for the relevant district duty office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company under the Commercial Act, submitted with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and supporting capital contribution evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or blocked escrow account requirement is imposed by the Korean Commercial Act. The Articles of Incorporation must state the total capital and each member's contribution; all contributions must be subscribed and paid in before or at incorporation in a Korean bank or a designated foreign exchange bank. In-kind contributions must be fully delivered and, where required, supported by valuation or court inspection evidence. For a nonresident shareholder, inward remittance should be reported through a Foreign Exchange Bank, and if the investment is intended to be recognized as foreign direct investment, a Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification is required. There is no escrow amount blocked with the commercial registry; funds become available to the company after commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, THAT the formation report submitted by the incorporator, together with the Articles of Incorporation and all ancillary exhibits, is hereby received, reviewed and accepted in its entirety. The corporation, to be registered as KR_YUHANGHOESA, shall be formed as a Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company, under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, with its registered office located at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation within the Republic of Korea. RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the total membership subscriptions and paid-up capital set out in the Articles are ratified; each contributing member's interest is accepted in the subscribed proportion; and the aggregate contribution has been, or will immediately be, transferred to the company's designated bank account in lawful currency and shall remain available for corporate purposes only. RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the initial director or directors, and auditor if required or voluntarily appointed, be and are hereby appointed for the first statutory term; the representative director is authorized to exercise all powers vested under the Articles and applicable law and to bind the company alone or together with such other officer as the company may appoint. RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the registered office set out in the Articles is adopted as the company's statutory seat, and the representative director shall procure the lease, ownership or sublease evidence needed for the competent registry. RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the representative director and any two finance officers be and are hereby authorized to open, manage and close corporate bank accounts, to engage online payment providers, and to register electronic signature platform credentials; banking signatory authority may be delegated by written power of attorney. RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the corporate seal is adopted; the seal impression and digital certificate controller, if any, shall be safekept and every affixation of the corporate seal shall be logged. RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT counsel and the corporate service provider are authorized to prepare, notarize, e-file and pay all statutory incorporation registration tax, local education tax, and court fees, and to apply to the district court registry and the National Tax Service for all certificates and tax registrations necessary to commence lawful operations. RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the company's objects are confined to computer programming, cloud document automation, electronic signature authentication, legal technology software services and activities ancillary thereto. RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the directors shall maintain the commercial registration certificate, submit annual returns and tax filings, and keep the books of account in accordance with the External Audit Act and the Framework Act on International Taxation. RESOLVED, FINALLY, THAT any director or officer may make immaterial corrections to this resolution and execute such counterpart instruments as may be necessary to give full force and effect to the foregoing resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Structural Blueprint
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court where the registered office will be located; preliminary name search via the Supreme Court of Korea Irosarang electronic litigation portal and KIPRIS trademark search system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a nationwide search to confirm that the proposed English and Korean corporate names are not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or a prior trademark. Verify that the stated business purpose under ISIC 6201, namely cloud document automation and e-signature authentication, does not fall within a licensed, permit-regulated or government-consented activity under Korean law. If the search is clear, prepare a structural memorandum setting out the full Korean legal name, English rendition, office address, member identities, contribution amounts and governance powers. For nonresident founders, confirm whether the investment must be reported as foreign direct investment or only as a foreign exchange transaction. Retain the search results and all name evidence to accompany the notarization file. This pre-filing discipline reduces the risk of rejection at the registration stage.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation draft
Copy of passport or national identity document of every proposed member
Notarized power of attorney if representation is used
Letter of intent or draft lease for the registered office
Draft foreign direct investment or foreign exchange reporting note
Trademark and company name search results
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as too similar, immediately select two alternate names and repeat the search; no monetary cure is necessary. If a trademark opposition is identified, amend the English name or obtain a coexistence consent from the prior right holder before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean notary public appointed under the Notary Act, assisted by external corporate counsel; the deposit is made at a Foreign Exchange Bank or a Korean branch institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation, including the corporate name, purpose, total capital, contributions of each member, transfer restrictions on membership interests, registered office, method of representation, auditor or director provisions, fiscal year and succession clauses. All members or their lawful proxies must sign before the notary. The notary will verify identity, capacity and comprehension, and will certify that the articles are lawful. Simultaneously, each capital contribution, whether cash or in kind, must be paid in or delivered. For cash contributions, obtain a bank deposit certificate or remittance receipt from the receiving bank. For nonresident members, the remittance should be credited to a Korean bank and retained under the foreign investment identification system. After notarization, retain the certified original and two certified copies to submit with the registration application.
required_dossiers: Korean-language Articles of Incorporation signed by all members
Identity and passport copies of all members and proxies
Capital subscription schedule and payment receipt
In-kind contribution appraisal report if applicable
Notary fee receipt
Power of attorney and certified signature specimen for any proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to certify due to defective provisions, circulate a revised execution draft, obtain new signatures and pay an additional notarial fee. If a foreign member's signature lacks apostille or consular legalization required by Korean private international law, obtain the appropriate certification and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration at the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court, including the electronic registration portal operated by the Supreme Court of Korea for the filing of the incorporation of the Yuhan Hoesa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after notarization, submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company together with the notarized Articles and the required exhibits. The filing may be made electronically through the court e-registration system or in person at the registry window. The registry will examine legal capacity, purpose, contribution payment evidence, office location and the consent of directors and auditor to accept their offices. Upon approval, pay the registration tax, local education tax and registration fee; the registrar then records the company as existing and issues an official certificate of registered matters, the corporate seal registration certificate, and an electronic number for subsequent filings. The certificate of registered matters must be verified and downloaded for all later tax, bank and commercial steps.
required_dossiers: Application form for incorporation registration
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate or bank receipt proving payment of capital contributions
Consent to appointment signed by each director and auditor
Resident registration or passport copies of the representative and auditor
Power of attorney and identity of the filing agent
Office lease or letter of consent from the owner of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an order for correction, supply all missing documents through the electronic supplement function within the stated cure period, normally one to seven days. If registration is rejected or dismissed, an immediate appeal may be filed under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, or a corrected application may be filed anew without losing prior name protection if the company name is unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Identification with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax online portal or the tax office having jurisdiction over the company's business premises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the legal deadline from commercial registration, submit the corporate business registration application to the National Tax Service under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Corporate Tax Act. The tax office will issue the business registration certificate and corporate tax identification number. For a LegalTech SaaS company providing cloud document automation and e-signature services, the activities are taxable electronic services, so the company must register for electronic tax invoice issuance, establish bookkeeping, and choose the appropriate taxable period. Secure a tax representative if the representative director is nonresident and has no Korean tax domicile. Submit the lease certificate, registered matters certificate and bank statement to verify the actual business place. Contest any valuation or taxpayer classification before commencing billing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business premise lease certificate or occupancy certificate
Bank account certificate and paid-in capital evidence
Passport copies of all directors and the tax representative
Corporate seal certificate or legalized seal impression
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends the application due to missing premises evidence, submit a corrected lease ledger or an additional floor plan and property consent. Late filing penalties can be reduced through voluntary correction; if the assigned tax office is wrong, transfer the file to the proper office and obtain written confirmation of the transfer date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Declaration and Activation of Banking and Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Invest Korea One-Stop Service or a Foreign Exchange Bank; for payment rails, the licensed commercial bank where the corporate account is opened.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If any member is nonresident and the investment qualifies as foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, file the FDI report with Invest Korea or a designated foreign exchange bank before or within 20 days after the inward remittance. Present the capital remittance certificate, the certificate of incorporation and the proof of foreign ownership to obtain an FDI certificate which permits preferential treatment and subsequent current account operations. Open the operational corporate bank account using the certificate of registered matters, corporate seal and director identities; connect the account to Stripe, credit card acquirers or third-party payment processors only after bank AML/KYC approval. Verify that the bank's compliance team accepts the corporate resolution and digital signatory mandates, complete beneficial ownership declarations, and maintain records of all payment providers for tax and audit purposes.
required_dossiers: FDI report form and remittance receipt
Certificate of registered matters of KR_YUHANGHOESA
Notarized Articles and current corporate resolution
Passports of the nonresident shareholders and representative director
Beneficial ownership declaration for the bank
Corporate seal certificate and bank mandate form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced KYC, provide a source-of-funds explanation, corporate ownership chart and bank reference letter. If the FDI report is rejected, file an amended report with the responsible ministry or KOTRA within the statutory correction period and re-validate the inward remittance date. If no FDI recognition is sought, maintain a foreign exchange settlement report to enable future dividend remittance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 is a pure digital software and legal technology service; the entity has no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly or warehousing activities, and therefore holds no industrial operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - No EIA registration, full impact assessment or prior environmental screening is required for cloud software operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - There is no wastewater discharge point, air emission source, VOC-emitting process or hazardous waste stream requiring quantitative compliance thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for an industrial fire or civil defense permit; however, the company must observe ordinary occupational safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act at its commercial office, and the lessor's building occupancy certificate and fire safety certificate should be maintained in the company file.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, acting through the HomeTax electronic tax administration portal (www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) operates the UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance system for export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) incorporated in South Korea, the foreign non-resident entity or its domestic tax representative must apply to the district tax office under the NTS for a Business Registration Certificate (Business Registration Number, 10 digits) using the statutory Application for Business Registration, within 20 days after the business commences. The application must be filed with: (1) certified articles of incorporation and corporate certificate demonstrating completed incorporation registration; (2) evidence of the domestic place of business, typically the lease agreement or ownership certificate; (3) certified Korean-language translation of the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation or equivalent proof of legal existence, apostilled/consularized if required; (4) photographic identification and passport copy of the foreign legal representative; (5) a power of attorney appointing a licensed tax accountant (sesamusa) or a domestic tax representative where the foreign entity has no resident officer; and (6) any banking due diligence documents evidencing the initial capital contribution if the entity maintains a corporate bank account. The NTS issues the Business Registration Number through the HomeTax portal, and that number functions simultaneously as the national Tax Identification Number for corporate income tax, the VAT registration ID, and the electronic tax invoice identifier. Foreign non-resident entities without a domestic place of business that supply electronic services or other Korean-source supplies are required to complete the simplified VAT registration procedure available to foreign business operators through the HomeTax portal and must appoint a domestic tax representative for VAT and corporate income tax compliance; the NTS will issue a separate non-resident tax registration number rather than a domestic Business Registration Certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic Korean corporation taxed at the entity level on worldwide income under the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act and local income tax acts; pass-through treatment is not available under Korean law. The entity is also an independent VAT taxable person subject to the Value-Added Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification - Korea does not operate any check-the-box or comparable elective entity-classification regime. A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation. The only relevant election is the Korean consolidated corporate tax return regime, available under Articles 76-2 to 76-8 of the Corporate Income Tax Act to a fully owned domestic subsidiary and a qualifying resident parent corporation; this is not a pass-through election. Hybrid mismatch and other anti-avoidance elective mechanisms are governed by the Adjustment of International Taxes Act and do not permit a taxpayer to change its Korean tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW; there is no general registration exemption threshold. Every supplier making taxable supplies of goods or services in South Korea must register for VAT. A simplified taxable person computation scheme is available to small businesses with aggregate annual turnover or revenue not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but that is a computational relief and does not eliminate the registration obligation. Foreign non-resident electronic services suppliers making B2C supplies to Korean customers must register under the simplified foreign business operator VAT registration procedure; there is no turnover threshold for that registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory national electronic tax invoice system administered by NTS through HomeTax and NTS-certified API/EDI service providers. A VAT-registered supplier must issue an electronic tax invoice to the recipient no later than the day following the time of supply and transmit the invoice data to the NTS; the transaction is then centrally validated and cross-matched by the NTS. The system is not a Latin-American-style real-time digital fiscal stamping clearance system, but it imposes mandatory daily transmission and acceptance confirmation. Anti-fraud controls include centralized invoice number audit, recipient confirmation obligations, and penalty surcharges for non-issuance, delayed issuance, missing transmission, or false invoice data. Supplies made through credit card or payment gateways such as Stripe or credit card acquirers additionally generate transaction-level data that NTS may reconcile against VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for goods exported to foreign countries under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act when the goods are physically cleared from South Korea through the Korea Customs Service and formally exported under a customs export declaration. Zero-rating also applies to services supplied to non-resident recipients where the service is consumed, used, or exploited wholly outside South Korea, and to qualifying international transportation and ocean/air freight services. For export zero-rating to be substantiated, the Korean supplier must be registered for VAT, the transaction must be evidenced by a commercial invoice issued to the foreign purchaser, the goods must depart Korea under KCS customs clearance, and the export proceeds must be repatriated in a lawful foreign-exchange transaction within the statutory period. A Yuhan Hoesa engaged in LegalTech SaaS, cloud document automation, and e-signature services may zero-rate its exported digital subscriptions and electronic-signature services only if it can establish that the non-resident recipient received and used the services outside Korea, invoicing is made to the overseas customer, and the consideration is received through a licensed foreign-exchange bank or permitted payment rail.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: UNI-PASS Customs Export Declaration Certificate (Export Clearance Report) issued by the Korea Customs Service for each export shipment
Commercial Invoice and Packing List executed by the Korean exporter and addressed to the foreign buyer
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment of goods from a Korean port/airport to a foreign destination

Foreign Currency Inward Remittance Certificate or Export Proceeds Confirmation issued by an authorized foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, showing receipt of export consideration in convertible foreign currency
Export Performance Confirmation Certificate issued by the handling foreign exchange bank or Korea Customs Service where required for the export transaction to prove the foreign-exchange earning event
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS VAT audit teams cross-check export zero-rating refund claims against Korea Customs Service export declarations, bank foreign-exchange receipts, and corporate income tax records. If the required export declaration, shipping documents, or foreign-exchange repatriation evidence are missing, unverified, or fraudulent, the zero-rating is rejected and the 10% VAT is assessed retroactively on the export supply, with interest and late-payment surcharges. The NTS may impose aggravated additional tax penalties up to 40% of the unlawfully refunded or understated tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including the 40% unfair refund/unjust enrichment penalty, the 20% underreporting penalty, and the 10% non-filing penalty, plus daily statutory interest at 0.022% for overdue tax debts. Where fraudulent tax invoices or forged export declarations are used to obtain an export VAT refund, criminal prosecution may be pursued under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with seizure and clawback of the refunded amount and additional monetary penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but regulated foreign exchange environment under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account remittances, including SaaS subscription fees and legal contract automation services, are freely allowed and may be settled through a licensed foreign exchange bank; the requirement is a transaction report and an appropriate purpose code rather than a prior license. Capital account movements, including inbound foreign direct investment into a Yuhan Hoesa, are subject to notification through the Ministry of Economy and Finance and Bank of Korea. In practice, FDI funds can be remitted under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; after investment report filing and business registration are recorded, capital can be converted into KRW by a licensed foreign exchange bank, subject to beneficial owner identification. There is no surrender requirement for export receivables; exporters may keep foreign currency in domestic foreign currency deposit accounts. Profit remittances are treated as current transactions and can be wired abroad as dividends after corporate governance documentation and tax compliance are completed; the practical brake is documentation-heavy, not a currency shortage. The main hurdles are verifying the underlying trade/capital nature, proving the UBO chain, calculating withholding tax (20 percent dividend withholding unless reduced by treaty), and satisfying mandatory reporting to tax, customs, and foreign exchange authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and MOEF regulations, export proceeds for goods must be received within five years from the export declaration date unless a longer deferred-payment period is separately approved; there is no mandatory conversion ratio, meaning 0 percent of export foreign currency receipts must be surrendered to the Bank of Korea, and the exporter may retain the proceeds in a resident foreign currency deposit at a licensed foreign exchange bank. Receipts must be settled through a licensed bank, purpose-coded, and overdue collection beyond the statutory window requires filing a report to the foreign exchange bank and MOEF.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account and Business Operational Account
KRW Settlement Account with Export Receipt and Trade Services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business or Payoneer are not licensed foreign exchange banks in South Korea and cannot replace a domestic Tier-1 bank for FDI capital custody, KRW conversion, export proceeds collection, trade settlement, or statutory corporate banking. They may be used only as ancillary payment processors for low-value SaaS/e-commerce collections, but all treasury money must ultimately be swept into an account at a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. Legal constraint: under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only foreign exchange banks and registered institutions may conduct foreign exchange business for a Korean corporate entity; offshore EMI account numbers do not satisfy the bank of record requirement for a Yuhan Hoesa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa, physical appearance of the statutory representative director at a Korean bank branch is effectively mandatory for initial corporate account opening. Korean banks are not generally open to fully remote onboarding of a foreign-owned LLC, and consular proxy opening is not accepted as a substitute. The representative director, and usually a second authorized signatory, must appear in person with original government-issued identification, corporate seal or equivalent proof, business registration certificate, and a board resolution naming account signatories. Some banks may permit a video interview and remote signature verification after an initial in-person visit or after apostilled powers of attorney are reviewed, but the compliance committee will still require direct branch verification for account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO transparency is weak because the foreign shareholder chain or offshore parent company obscures the natural-person controller of the Korean LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide current apostilled register of members for every entity in the ownership chain, structural chart to natural persons, certified passports of all UBOs, UBO declaration forms, bank reference letters from the parent's primary bank, source-of-funds evidence for subscribed capital, and audited financial statements or accountant confirmation for shareholder wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: LegalTech contract automation may be misread by the bank as unlicensed legal practice, as a sanctions-exposed legal services business, or as an industry requiring a professional license.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a product brochure, technical documentation, white-label agreements, and executed customer contracts showing cloud document automation and e-signature authentication only; include the ISIC 6201 business classification certificate, a Korean legal opinion confirming no statutory license is needed, a sanctions screening report of the client roster, and the entity's internal compliance policy covering electronic signature verification and anti-money-laundering screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank sees shell or substance risk because a foreign-invested LLC with an overseas director sends and receives high volumes of SaaS payments without clear local operational footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a valid Korean office lease or ownership title, local payroll or contractor records, business registration certificate, monthly operational expense invoices, telecommunications and utility bills, corporate minutes approving treasury signatories, and if applicable a virtual office arrangement supported by actual staff, client-facing activity, and cloud infrastructure in Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency Stripe/credit-card collection and outbound vendor payments create a transaction-profile red flag because the bank cannot reconcile the underlying SaaS subscription economy with invoices and FX receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the verified Stripe merchant agreement, monthly settlement statements mapped to invoices, e-signature subscription contracts, a revenue ledger, exception report for chargebacks or refunds, matching SWIFT credits to invoice numbers, sanctions screening logs, board resolution appointing the treasury manager, and dual-approval signatory control documentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route is to open a foreign-currency FDI receipt account at a Tier-1 Korean foreign exchange bank after filing an investment notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (via KOTRA or the receiving bank). The foreign investor remits by SWIFT MT103 using the exact corporate legal name, Korean business registration number, investment notification number, direct-investment foreign exchange purpose code, and the bank's foreign-currency intermediary details. No sanctioned bank or unlicensed intermediary may be used in the chain. After the remittance is credited and matched to the FDI notification, the bank performs capital verification and permits conversion into KRW through an onshore USD/KRW spot trade. The Yuhan Hoesa must complete share subscription, board approval, registration in the Korean commercial registry, and any post-closing notification to KOTRA. Necessary evidence includes the share subscription agreement, articles of incorporation, bank foreign-currency deposit certificate, capital injection board resolution, and audited proof of funds if requested.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For SaaS subscriptions, cloud hosting, legal data feeds, marketing procurement, and intercompany service fees, the principal clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct corporate wire transfers with the correct foreign exchange purpose code and underlying invoice or contract. For higher-value physical procurement, commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) and documentary collections (DP/DA) are acceptable rails if transport and trade documents are available. Domestic KRW disbursements use the Korean domestic payment and settlement rails operated by the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute (KFTC). All outbound payments must pass bank sanctions screening, be supported by board-approved disbursement policy, and be reported to the bank with source documents for audit trail purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank for term-matched USD/KRW receipts and payables, supported by the underlying SaaS export or import invoices
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps permitted for genuine economic exposures such as intercompany loans, hosting fees, and capital transactions, with the bank verifying the underlying cash flow
Vanilla European FX options (forwards and collars structures) used by the treasury to hedge expected USD and KRW cash flows without speculative intent

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not a mainstream onshore hedge for a Korean operating Yuhan Hoesa; they are reserved for non-resident counterparties or specific offshore market-access scenarios and cannot replace economic-exposure hedging with a licensed Korean bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 1100 series) including tax base adjustment statement and statutory financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a December fiscal year-end, by 31 March of the following year, with a one-month extension to 30 April when the return is prepared by a licensed Korean tax attorney or certified public accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax, underreporting penalties up to 40%, and late-payment interest of 0.022% per day from the statutory due date. After 30 days from a final tax demand, the NTS may seize assets; six consecutive months of unreported business activity permits cancellation of the business registration and, ultimately, court-initiated deletion from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax (local inhabitant tax) return and payment on corporate income tax payable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Si/Gun/Gu local government tax department, with electronic filing available through NTS HomeTax where integrated collection applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the national corporate income tax return; for a calendar-year company, by 31 March, extendable to 30 April when the national corporate tax return is filed with a qualified tax professional
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax delinquency surcharge of 3% for unpaid local income tax after the due date, late-payment interest of 0.022% per day, and an underreporting penalty of 10% of the unpaid local tax. Persistent non-payment may trigger compulsory seizure of bank accounts and receivables and eventual cancellation of the business place registration.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to 20 billion, 21% from KRW 20 billion to 300 billion; plus 10% local corporate income tax surtax on the national tax, aggregating to a 26.4% top effective headline on large tax bases
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives include R&D tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, with up to 30% for qualifying national strategic technology research and 20-25% for ordinary qualifying R&D; tax reductions and exemptions for high-technology foreign-invested companies in free economic zones under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; SME and venture enterprise tax relief; and technology transfer/royalty income relief equal to a 50% corporate tax reduction for qualifying self-developed intellectual property, which operates in practice as a patent-box equivalent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Payable Return filed under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act; mandatory electronic filing through the NTS HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr), including the Foreign-Related Transaction Report and financial statement schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end the return is due by 31 March of the following calendar year. One additional month is available on application for audited foreign financial statements, and the foreign-related transaction schedule is due together with the return, not in the ordinary extension period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1a - Entity and shareholder identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Business Registration Number, Yuhan Hoesa designation, registered address, resident status, fiscal year end, and non-resident shareholder schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For KR_YUHANGHOESA, report the entity as a Korean-resident domestic corporation even when wholly foreign-owned; enter the foreign investor's country, shareholding percentage, foreign investment report number, and ultimate beneficial owner details. Do not classify as a foreign corporation merely because shareholders are non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2a - Place of effective management and principal place of business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address of the head office or place of effective management, principal business premises, and automated digital infrastructure location in Korea.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose where board meetings and management decisions occur; if automation servers and e-signature authentication are hosted in Korea, state whether the server footprint and employees constitute a domestic permanent establishment. For a Korean-incorporated LLC, management exercised in Korea is presumptive residency; foreign-resident directors should note the absence of foreign management to prevent false PE allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 - Business scope and tax accounting method
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Industry code, activity description, principal activity of cloud document automation and e-signature SaaS, and revenue recognition policy for subscriptions and contract automation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For ISIC 6201, describe the source of Korean income and separately classify software licensing, data processing, and electronic authentication service components for withholding analysis; do not characterize SaaS fees as non-reportable royalties unless a full transfer pricing analysis supports that regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 30 - Tax base after adjustments / loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after accounting adjustments, non-deductible expenses, transfer pricing adjustments, and NOL deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If claiming NOL, attach a reconciliation of the loss origin year and expiry; losses older than the permitted carryforward period must be added back. Apply arm's length adjustments to intercompany management, software license, and cloud hosting fees paid to non-resident affiliates; excessive royalties or management fees not supported by functions, assets, and risks are denied under the substance-over-form rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 41 / Line 42 - Tax credits, treaty withholdings, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax credits, domestic withholding credits, and foreign tax credit reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify that all dividends, interest, and royalties payable to non-resident shareholders have already been subjected to the statutory 22% aggregate withholding or to the reduced DTA rate only after the treaty application and Tax Residency Certificate have been filed; if foreign tax credits are claimed, attach actual evidence of overseas tax paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 70 - Representative director's declaration and signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement by the representative director that the return is accurate and complete, with company seal, digital certificate, and date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-resident representative director must sign through a registered Korean digital certificate; knowingly false declarations are deemed joint criminal conduct, and the director loses the limited-liability shield and becomes a target of NTS criminal referral and departure restriction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers per-day overdue surcharges on unpaid corporate tax capped at 15% under the Framework Act on National Taxes; underreported or unfaithfully filed returns attract 10%-20% of the underpaid tax as additional tax and 30%-40% for fraudulent omission; non-filing of the foreign-related transaction report attracts a separate per-transaction penalty; repeated or fraudulent non-filing is criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 2 years and fines up to 5 times the evaded tax.
